newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates close higher on nervousness.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates close higher on nervousness.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed 125 basis points higher at 19.0 percent on Tuesday, reflecting concerns over volatility before the July 6 mid-term elections and uncertainty over rate movements in the United States, dealers said.

"We are getting closer to July 2, when the (Federal Open Market Committee of the U.S. Federal Reserve) meets, and to July 6, when we get the elections, and the market is getting nervous and they want to keep liquid to cover themselves," said one analyst.
Dealers also said they expect a strong increase in primary rates at Banco de Mexico's Cetes auction that was held earlier in the day.

Mexico's bellwether 28-day Cetes rate is seen rising 71 basis points to 19.02 percent at the auction, and rates are also seen rising at longer terms, according to a Reuters' survey of nine Cetes dealers.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed 60 basis points higher at 19.90 percent.
